verdict.rationale: Inngest documents step memoization: completed steps are checkpointed and not re-run when a function retries or resumes. That covers part of the exactly-once step story, keeping side effects such as charges or sends from repeating on retry. Nothing in the pack documents idempotency keys or event deduplication for duplicate triggers. Rate-limiting and concurrency keys are adjacent controls and earn no credit here. Missing for 10: documented idempotency keys or event-level deduplication for duplicate triggers, explicit exactly-once guarantees for steps, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a backend developer, idempotency keys and exactly-once step semantics stop duplicate triggers from double-charging or double-sending

citations.quote: Put side effects, API calls, sleeps, waits, and function invocations in steps so Inngest can memoize results, retry failures independently, and resume long-running work from the last successful checkpoint.
If the process dies at step 7 of 12, the agent picks up at step 7 — not step 1.
